title: High Molecular Weight DNA Extraction from Frozen Nematodes
author: Manuela Kieninger
materials: HMW gDNA Tissue Lysis Buffer
Proteinase
LysisMix buffer
Monarch pestle tube
ThermoMixer
2 mL LoBind tube
1000 µL wide-bore tip
Monarch Protein Separation Solution
Put the sample on ice for 5 min.
Invert at 20 rpm for 1 to 3 min. We use ThermoFisher's HulaMixer (cat# 15920D) set only for orbital rotation.
Leave the sample on ice for 10 min.
Invert on wheel or rocker at 7 rpm for 5 to 7 min. We use ThermoFisher's HulaMixer (cat# 15920D) set only for orbital rotation.
Carefully invert 2 to 3 times.
Put the tube in the ThermoMixer at 56°C and 300 rpm for 5 min.
Let the DNA elute further in ThermoMixer for 30 min at 37°C and 300 rpm.
Flash freeze in liquid nitrogen.
Follow the manufacturer's instructions to complete the Qubit.
Invert at 20 rpm for 1 to 3 min. We use ThermoFisher's HulaMixer (cat# 15920D) set only for orbital rotation.
Invert on wheel or rocker at 7 rpm for 5 to 7 min. We use ThermoFisher's HulaMixer (cat# 15920D) set only for orbital rotation.
Follow the manufacturer's instructions to complete the Qubit.

steps.title: Prepare LysisMix Buffer
steps.instruction: Per sample combine 600 µL HMW gDNA Tissue Lysis Buffer with 20 µL Proteinase K; mix at room temperature, then keep on ice (master mix possible).

steps.title: Add LysisMix to Pellet
steps.instruction: Add 50 µL cold LysisMix to the 1.5 mL tube containing the frozen nematode pellet and keep the tube on ice.

steps.title: Transfer to Pestle Tube
steps.instruction: If the pellet is not already in a Monarch pestle tube, transfer it to a 1.5 mL microfuge tube that fits the pestle.

steps.title: Homogenize with Pestle
steps.instruction: Perform at least 30 up‑down motions with the pestle, turning it in one direction only; allow the pellet to thaw slightly on ice before homogenization if possible.

steps.title: Add Remaining LysisMix
steps.instruction: Add 550 µL LysisMix buffer to the homogenized sample (total volume ≈ 630 µL).

steps.title: Digest Sample
steps.instruction: Transfer the entire ~630 µL to a 2 mL LoBind tube, incubate at 56 °C in a ThermoMixer at 750 rpm for 15 min, then reduce to 550 rpm for the remainder of the lysis (total 1.5 h); mix with a 1000 µL wide‑bore tip.

steps.title: Extend Lysis if Needed
steps.instruction: After 1.5 h, examine the lysate; if intact worms remain, continue incubation at 56 °C, 550 rpm, checking every 30 min up to a total of 2–4 h. Lysate may be stored at 4 °C overnight after this step.

steps.title: Post‑Lysis Heat Step
steps.instruction: Return the tube to the ThermoMixer for an additional 10 min at 56 °C, 550 rpm.

steps.title: Clarify Lysate
steps.instruction: Spin 5 min at 2500 rcf, retain the supernatant while leaving 30 µL behind; transfer the supernatant to a new 1.5 mL LoBind tube and add 30 µL HMW gDNA Tissue Lysis Buffer to restore the original volume.

steps.title: Protein Separation
steps.instruction: Add 300 µL cold Monarch Protein Separation Solution, invert immediately, then spin at room temperature at 16 000 rcf for 25 min (or longer until two stable phases are visible).

steps.title: Collect Upper Phase
steps.instruction: Carefully pipette the entire upper aqueous phase into a new 2 mL LoBind tube using slow pipetting to avoid disturbing the lower phase.

steps.title: Bind DNA to Beads
steps.instruction: Add 3 Monarch DNA Capture Beads to the aqueous phase, then add 550 µL Isopropanol and invert 20 times immediately.

steps.title: Remove Supernatant
steps.instruction: Discard the liquid without disturbing the beads (DNA is now bound to the beads).

steps.title: Optional Isopropanol Precipitation
steps.instruction: If DNA fails to bind, add 10 µL 3 M NaAc pH 5.2 and 200 µL additional Isopropanol to the saved supernatant, mix by 40 inversions, and centrifuge at 4 °C (speed as per kit instructions).

steps.title: First Wash
steps.instruction: Add 500 µL Monarch gDNA Wash Buffer to the beads, invert to mix, then remove the wash buffer with a tip without disturbing the beads.

steps.title: Elution Preparation
steps.instruction: Transfer the beads to a 2 mL tube, add 200 µL Monarch gDNA Elution Buffer II, avoid drying the beads, and short‑spin 1 s to remove excess liquid.

steps.title: Check Wool‑like Precipitate
steps.instruction: Inspect the wash buffer for any wool‑like material; if present, it can be saved and eluted separately (note lower purity).

steps.title: Bead Wash for Elution
steps.instruction: Place the beads in a bead retainer inside a 1.5 mL LoBind tube, add 50 µL Monarch gDNA Elution Buffer II on top, spin 30 s at 12 000 rcf, then pipette‑mix 20 times up‑and‑down with a wide‑bore tip.

steps.title: Overnight Elution
steps.instruction: Mix gently with a wide‑bore tip and incubate at room temperature overnight to elute DNA.

steps.title: Second Day Mixing
steps.instruction: The next day, pipette‑mix the bead suspension with a wide‑bore tip at least 20 times.

steps.title: RNase Treatment
steps.instruction: Add 10 µL RNase A and mix well with a wide‑bore tip.

steps.title: Grow Worms for Pellet
steps.instruction: Grow nematodes on four 10 cm NGMA plates seeded with OP50 to obtain a pellet of 40–80 mg; for multiple pellets scale plates proportionally (e.g., three pellets → twelve plates); after growth, wash all worms from plates into a single conical tube.

steps.title: First Wash with Cold M9
steps.instruction: When plates are starved, wash worms off each plate with cold M9 into a 15 or 50 mL conical (use 10 mL cold M9 per 2 plates).

steps.title: Centrifuge First Wash
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 2000 rpm for 8 min with brake speed 3; let the pellet sit on ice 2 min; aspirate supernatant, leaving 5–10 mL to avoid losing worms.

steps.title: Wash with M9 + Tween (First)
steps.instruction: Add 20 mL cold M9 containing 0.01 % Tween, centrifuge 2000 rpm 8 min brake 3, settle on ice 2 min, then aspirate supernatant (change tips between samples).

steps.title: Repeat Tween Washes
steps.instruction: Repeat the M9 + Tween wash two additional times for a total of three washes.

steps.title: Final M9 Wash
steps.instruction: Add 20 mL cold M9, centrifuge 2000 rpm 8 min brake 3; aspirate supernatant leaving approximately 1 mL M9.

steps.title: Transfer Pellet to Tubes
steps.instruction: Transfer the pellet with a Pasteur pipette to labeled 1.7 mL microfuge tubes that accommodate the Monarch pestle; if the tube fits the pestle, no further transfer is needed.

steps.title: Spin and Remove Supernatant
steps.instruction: Spin at 2000 rpm for 5 min; if supernatant is not clear or pellet is not sharp, spin again; remove as much supernatant as possible.

steps.title: Weigh Pellet
steps.instruction: Weigh each pellet (target 40–80 mg) using a calibrated scale, record the weight on the tube.

steps.title: Preserve Wash Supernatant
steps.instruction: Keep the removed supernatant in a separate microfuge tube in case DNA fails to bind to beads later.

steps.title: Optional Bead Retainer Setup
steps.instruction: Place a labeled bead retainer into a collection tube, pour beads into the retainer, then insert the retainer into a new 1.5 mL DNA LoBind tube (pre‑pares for later bead handling).

steps.title: Alternative Plate‑to‑Conical Transfer
steps.instruction: Add 5 mL cold M9 to plate 1, swirl, pour into plate 2, swirl, pour into the conical; repeat with another 5 mL M9 (alternative washing method).

steps.title: Additional Wash Buffer
steps.instruction: Add another 500 µL Monarch gDNA Wash Buffer to the pellet and invert to mix.

steps.title: Quantify DNA Yield
steps.instruction: Take 2 µL of the eluate for a Qubit Broad Range assay and 1 µL for a NanoDrop (or equivalent); ensure NanoDrop concentration is ≤ 2 × Qubit, A260/280 = 1.8–2.0, A260/A230 = 2.0–2.2.

steps.title: Prepare for TapeStation
steps.instruction: Use the required amount of sample for a TapeStation run with the Genomic DNA Reagents.

steps.title: High‑Throughput Plate Washing
steps.instruction: If many plates, arrange them in two rows; add 5 mL M9 to each top‑row plate, swirl, pour onto the corresponding bottom‑row plate; repeat a second time; then decant the combined M9 into a 50 mL conical.

steps.title: Split Pellet for Multiple Tubes
steps.instruction: If generating multiple pellets, transfer material dropwise to each tube to distribute the pellet equally.

steps.title: Expected DNA Quality
steps.instruction: The final DNA should show a sharp high‑molecular‑weight band/peak; DIN > 7.5 and > 50 % of fragments > 15 kb.
